Impute zeros in compositional data

impute_zeros.Rd

Replace zeros with small positive values using various imputation methods. This is necessary for log-ratio transformations which require non-zero values.

Usage

impute_zeros(
  x,
  method = c("multiplicative", "additive", "dl"),
  delta = NULL,
  preserve_structural = FALSE,
  structural_threshold = 0.8
)

Arguments

x

A simp_composition or simp_cover object

method

Imputation method:

  • "multiplicative": Multiplicative replacement (default)

  • "additive": Simple additive replacement

  • "dl": Detection limit replacement

delta

Replacement value. If NULL, automatically determined based on method. For multiplicative, uses 0.65 times minimum non-zero value.

preserve_structural

Logical; if TRUE, don't impute zeros that appear to be structural (default FALSE)

structural_threshold

Threshold for structural zeros (default 0.8)

Value

Object with imputed values

References

Martin-Fernandez, J.A., Barcelo-Vidal, C., Pawlowsky-Glahn, V. (2003) Dealing with zeros and missing values in compositional data sets using nonparametric imputation. Mathematical Geology, 35(3), 253-278.

Examples

x <- simp_composition(
  matrix(c(0.4, 0.4, 0.2, 0,
           0.5, 0.3, 0.2, 0,
           0.3, 0.5, 0, 0.2), nrow = 3, byrow = TRUE),
  components = c("sp1", "sp2", "sp3", "sp4")
)

# Multiplicative replacement
impute_zeros(x)

# Additive with custom delta
impute_zeros(x, method = "additive", delta = 0.001)
